title: Compacter shared fast factors versus Mirror modulation
hypothesis: Mirror codes over shared Compacter slow weights and fast-factor bases can represent aligned multi-task adapter updates with fewer bytes while preserving task quality; independent task updates may require native per-task fast factors.
physical_object: one frozen 16×16 linear map plus shared Compacter slow basis
mirror_coordinate: per-task scalar modulation of shared rank-one/Kronecker fast-factor atoms
controls: native Compacter shared slow + per-task fast factors
shared atom basis plus Mirror scalar codes
generic coefficient code over same atoms

development.allowed: validate Kronecker factor shapes, support fitting, task interference and serialized payload accounting

storage.authority: actual serialized inference payload bytes including shared bases and all task coefficients/factors

success_gate: Aligned tasks: Mirror/generic atom code NRMSE <=0.01 and payload <=70% of native Compacter; Mirror-specific value additionally requires >=10% quality/byte improvement over generic coefficients.
failure_gate: Mirror NRMSE >0.05 or independent-task cross-task interference >0.25; generic coefficient match means no Mirror-specific gain.
amendments: Development revealed that the initial serializer double-counted W and aligned targets used four independent atom coefficients while Mirror used one. Before fresh access, aligned targets were fixed to one scalar over one shared atom direction and serialization was corrected to charge W/bases/codes once. Earlier development rows are exploratory and retained.
boundaries: Compacter is prior art and mandatory direct control
Logical combinations are not capacity without measured held-out quality
